say: In this module you run a growth audit, price and scope the work so it stays profitable, and package your experiments into case studies that win clients or a growth role.

say: A growth audit is a short, fixed-scope project: a baseline funnel, the tracking gaps, and three recommended experiments. It starts with a discovery call. Ask: what would make the next 90 days a success?

panel.heading: Questions for the discovery call
items: Goal: what would make 90 days a success?
Customers: who buys, why, why do they leave?
Funnel: first contact to payment
Data: what is tracked, who can export?
Resources and past tests

say: Ask who buys most often, why they choose you, and why people leave. Then map what really happens between first contact and payment.

say: Ask what is tracked today and who can export it, what budget and help there is, and what they have tried before.
Talk for less than a third of the call, and summarise back what you heard.

say: Ask to be added with the lowest role that works, such as Viewer in Google Analytics, and take a CSV export of payments rather than a dashboard login.

panel.heading: Getting data access safely
items: Lowest role that works, e.g. Viewer
CSV export of payments, not a login
Agree in writing how data is stored
Remove access when the project ends

say: Agree in writing what data you will see and how you will store it, and remove access at the end. Payment exports are personal data under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, so keep them in a protected account with two-step verification.

say: Never accept a client's personal passwords or OTPs. Role-based access protects both of you.

say: For example, Zainab owns a ready-to-wear brand in Abuja and says her ads stopped working. Last month her ads got 6,000 link clicks, but GA4 shows only 2,100 sessions.

panel.heading: Zainab's ads were working after all
items: 6,000 clicks, only 2,100 sessions
Slow home page on mobile data
45 WhatsApp orders never counted
True CAC about 2,860 naira, not 5,000

say: So her 300,000 naira of ads brought 105 orders. True CAC is about 2,860 naira, not the 5,000 she calculated. The ads were fine. The leaks were a slow page, missing WhatsApp tracking and weak retention.

say: Price from your own numbers, built from what you need to earn, the hours you can bill, and your costs. For example, Kemi sets her rate at 15,000 naira an hour.
She estimates 20 hours: the discovery call, data cleaning, the funnel and cohort work, the report, and the presentation. That is 300,000 naira.
She adds a 15% buffer for revisions and delays, and quotes 345,000 naira for a three-week audit.
She takes 50%, which is 172,500 naira, before work starts, and the rest on delivery of the report.

Your proposal lists exact deliverables, dates, what the client must provide, and exclusions, such as ad spend and paid tools. When a client asks for more, reply warmly: happy to help, I will send a short quote.

panel.heading: Protect yourself and the client
right: Accept pay only if sales grow

say: Never promise a growth percentage. Growth depends on stock, delivery and the owner's speed. And beware of new clients who overpay and ask for a refund of the difference. Confirm money has reached your account in your banking app before starting.

panel.heading: Protect yourself and the client
right: Accept pay only if sales grow

say: Employers want proof you can find a leak and tell the truth about the result. For example, Ada's case study starts with her baseline: 300 chats, 90 first orders, 30 percent. The insight: 18 of 30 lost chats asked about delivery days.

panel.heading: Ada's honest case study
items: Baseline: 300 chats, 90 orders, 30%
Insight: 18 of 30 lost chats asked delivery
Test: A 30% vs B 40%, 150 chats each
z about 1.82: promising, not significant
Decision: free, no complaints, adopted

say: For four weeks, new chats alternated between the old reply, A, and a quick reply, B. A converted 30 percent, B 40 percent.

panel.heading: Ada's honest case study
items: Baseline: 300 chats, 90 orders, 30%
Insight: 18 of 30 lost chats asked delivery
Test: A 30% vs B 40%, 150 chats each
z about 1.82: promising, not significant
Decision: free, no complaints, adopted

say: But z is about 1.82, below 1.96, so it is not significant. Because the change was free and caused no complaints, she adopted it and kept measuring.
This case study is strong precisely because it is honest.

say: To remember. Sell a fixed audit first, and count every channel, including WhatsApp orders, before judging CAC. Price from hours, rate and buffer, and take a deposit. Never guarantee growth. And report results honestly, including the ones that failed.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Sell a fixed audit first
Count every channel before judging CAC
Price = hours x rate + buffer
Never guarantee growth
Include borderline and failed results
